title: Sending Signals with Light and Sound
seo_title: Grade 1 Signals Worksheets: Send Messages with Light and Sound
standard_text: Use tools and materials to design and build a device that uses light or sound to solve the problem of communicating over a distance.
meta_desc: Free grade 1 science worksheets on signals (NGSS 1-PS4-4): flashlights, drums, whistles, codes and cup phones for sending messages far away. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_big: Send messages with light or sound.
key_sub: Flash a light or bang a drum. Agree on a code first.
body_html:
How to think about it

We can send messages far away.

  • Use light: flashlight, lighthouse.
  • Use sound: drum, whistle, bell.
  • Agree on a code first.
Example

Code: 1 flash = yes, 2 flashes = no. You see 2 flashes.

Count them.

Answer: no

Example

Your friend is around a corner. Light or sound?

Sound goes around corners.

Answer: sound

Common mistakes

  • Using a light signal when your friend cannot see it.
  • Letting the string of a cup phone hang loose.
  • Sending a code your friend does not know.

faq.q: How can we send a message far away?
faq.a: With light, like a flashlight or a lighthouse, or with sound, like a drum, whistle or bell.

faq.q: When is light better? When is sound better?
faq.a: Light is good when your friend can see you, even in a noisy place. Sound is good around corners or through doors.
A flashlight code, a drum code or a cup-and-string phone with a tight string.
